author: FerreiraMatheus
body:
Because you only need to get some that work one time. It would make zero sense if you have 10% of chance to get the great amities, in about a month no one would be doing amities anymore. If Odie wants people to be interested in it for a long time, it must be hard to get. 

When you get the 40% critical, the hybrid damage, mana every turn, more elemental damage, and all you want, why would you continue to do amities?

But statistics are on our side. You'll eventually get all the amities you want, or close to that. That's the game. That's why you should do it.

author: Caelani920
body:
Since you're all talking Amities, I have a question that I haven't seen answered anywhere.

Example: Let's say I have a "Dominion" amity (increased stats while defending territory) on my DEFAULT loadout. Is that active all the time when people attack me in PvP, or must I put that on my PvP loadout?

The same question surrounds "Feebleness" (stats decreased while defending territory). If I equip that with my Raid loadout, does it always have zero effect (since I'm not in PvP while raiding), or do I have this malus active in PvP while I am raiding, or does it not apply to PvP at all, since those who attack my territory face me with my PvP loadout which would NOT have this malus?

Thanks for any light you could shed on this.

author: Palocos
body:
You said 2% are great. Ok, what percentage of ornate gear are you getting? 

I think the problem is you're underestimating how good average amities are. I think 50% of amities are useful. 5% extra orns is not great, but it is useful. 5% mana regeneration is not great but it can be very useful in hard endless. 15% extra elemental damage is not great, but it is always helpful. Now 40% extra crit damage is insane. 

The one thing I'll agree is that legendary and ornate amities usually suck because they come with a high chance of unbearable drawbacks.
